audit_findings.title: Pre-acquisition OE omits the current debt interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $48 million of identified acquisition-financing interest in the first six months of 2026 ($33 million Incremental Term Loan plus $15 million Senior Notes); Allison Off-Highway reported $26 million of segment operating profit and $1,379 million of sales for the same period; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The pre-acquisition OE anchor excludes acquired earnings and most acquisition financing costs, while post-acquisition cash, debt and shares define the valued equity claim.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 1, 2026, the Acquisition was completed for a purchase price of approximately $2,732 million, subject to certain adjustments, using a combination of cash on hand, the $500 million of proceeds from the issuance of the 5.875% Senior Notes 2033, $1,200 million of proceeds from the Incremental Term Loan, and $300 million borrowed under the Revolving Credit Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possibility. The omitted acquired earnings, incremental interest, taxes, integration spending and maintenance investment are collectively large enough to alter the OE anchor and potentially the valuation conclusion; their net direction cannot be established from segment operating profit alone.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct post-acquisition OE from the 2026 filings, including acquired operating cash generation, all incremental interest, taxes, recurring integration costs and maintenance investment, then rerun every scenario. Alternatively rerun a wholly pre-acquisition claim with consistently dated cash, debt and shares.

audit_findings.title: Acquired senior claims may be missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $1,157 million of acquired liabilities, including $298 million deferred taxes, $34 million finance leases, $38 million warranty liabilities and $338 million of other current and non-current liabilities; any uncaptured senior claim is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An obligation not represented in normalized OE or the equity bridge would reduce the residual value belonging to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the limited amount of time since closing the transaction, the preliminary allocation of the purchase price is not yet complete.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing now identifies the aggregate acquired liabilities, but the purchase-price allocation remains preliminary and $338 million of other liabilities is not sufficiently disaggregated for this review. Many listed liabilities may already flow through working capital or future OE, so subtracting them wholesale would double count; the record does not establish the amount, if any, omitted from value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each acquired liability in the final purchase-price allocation to its expected cash payments and treatment in normalized OE, separately identifying pensions, environmental obligations, restructuring, indemnities, deferred taxes and contingent consideration.

audit_findings.title: All cash is treated as distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: filed maximum $399 million, equal to computed $4.77 per diluted share; $368 million was in operating accounts and $331 million was held by foreign subsidiaries
audit_findings.mechanism: Any required, restricted or otherwise unavailable cash should be excluded from the cash added to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our principal uses of cash are operating expenses, capital expenditures, working capital needs, debt service, dividends on common stock, stock repurchases and strategic growth initiatives, including investments, acquisitions and collaborations.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable portion is unresolved, but even removing the entire $399 million would reduce the base value from $103.03 to approximately $98.26 per share and the bull value from $120.71 to approximately $115.94. That cannot reverse the conclusion at the $131.24 market price or make the shares satisfy the $72.12 buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating cash, restrictions and repatriation costs and add only excess cash in the next rerun; confirm that interest income associated with retained cash is treated consistently.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition costs may be asymmetrically retained
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $64 million of 2025 acquisition-related expense, with $47 million paid in 2025; a further $26 million of expense and $41 million of related payments were reported for the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining nonrecurring transaction costs depresses anchor OE, while removing costs that recur during integration overstates sustainable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, the Company recognized $ 64 million of acquisition-related expenses recorded in Selling, general and administrative in the Company's Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income, primarily consisting of consulting and legal fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The costs are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether or how the $64 million was adjusted in the $584.5 million OE anchor. A full $64 million pretax anchor adjustment is about 11% of anchor OE and would imply roughly $10.75 per share under the base operating-PV relationship before tax effects, while continuing 2026 costs could offset part of that benefit. Materiality and direction therefore remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $64 million line by line through the OE calculation, distinguish transaction costs from recurring integration expenditures, apply the associated tax effects and rerun OE using an explicit normalization schedule.

audit_findings.title: Expired hedge benefits may understate normalized interest
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $6 million of 2025 interest-rate-swap receipts; computed maximum base-value effect before tax is approximately $1.01 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in anchor OE, expired swap receipts reduce historical interest expense and overstate sustainable equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In September 2025, all of the Company's interest rate swap contracts reached maturity and were terminated.
audit_findings.explanation: The hedge expiration is demonstrated, although retention in OE still requires tracing. The full $6 million equals about 1.0% of the $584.5 million anchor and, even before tax, maps to only about $1.01 per share under the base valuation relationship. This is far below the $10.53 gap between the bull value and market price and cannot change the valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $6 million remains in anchor OE and, if so, remove it or replace it with interest calculated from the applicable unhedged debt terms in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement claims require explicit treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $4 million unfunded pension obligation plus $66 million unfunded OPEB obligation; computed legacy claim equals $0.84 per diluted share; acquired-plan exposure is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unfunded benefit claims reduce value if their future cash payments are neither captured in normalized OE nor recognized as a senior claim in the bridge; accounting credits can also inflate OE relative to cash cost.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the unfunded status of our defined benefit pension plans was $4 million and the unfunded status of our OPEB plan was $66 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The known $70 million legacy deficit alone is not material: a full direct deduction would be only $0.84 per share versus the $10.53 gap between bull value and market price. However, the treatment of benefit credits and cash payments in OE has not been reconciled, and the filing does not separately identify any acquired pension or OPEB deficit. Total materiality therefore remains unresolved rather than disproven.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile legacy and acquired pension and OPEB expense, credits, contributions, benefit payments, assets and obligations; recognize only the residual claim not already captured in normalized OE, then rerun if acquired-plan exposure is material.
